headline_marked: SMIC [[posts record $3B quarter]] and hikes wafer prices amid AI boom
headline: SMIC posts record $3B quarter and hikes wafer prices amid AI boom
summary: China's sole 7nm-class foundry saw revenue surge 36.1% year-on-year, with net profit nearly tripling. The company is increasing wafer prices for Q3.
details: SMIC has reported its first-ever $3 billion quarter, with revenue up 36.1% year-on-year and net profit nearly tripling to $479.2 million. The company's Co-CEO indicated that wafer prices will increase in the third quarter following negotiations.

The foundry operated at 93.7% utilization, exceeding its own guidance. This high demand is attributed to China's AI data center buildouts, which are increasingly relying on domestic chip production due to U.S. export controls restricting access to leading-edge foundries like TSMC and Samsung.

SMIC's gross margin rose to 25.3% from 20.1% in the previous quarter, surpassing its guided range of 20% to 22%. Wafer shipments increased by 14% quarter-on-quarter, with blended selling prices climbing 5.7%.

The surge in demand is primarily driven by AI chips other than CPUs and GPUs, including logic ICs, power-management parts, and optical transceiver components. SMIC's AI peripheral segment is expected to grow around 40% this quarter.

This performance marks a significant turnaround from 2023, when SMIC's utilization was around 68.1% and net profit fell over 60%. The company had been cutting prices to defend market share against new domestic capacity.

U.S. export controls have effectively created a protected market for SMIC, as Chinese AI accelerator demand is redirected inward. Beijing aims for 70% of silicon wafers to be sourced domestically this year, with local firms planning to spend significantly more on Chinese chips.

SMIC is the only Chinese foundry capable of mass-producing 7nm-class logic, making it the sole domestic supplier for key AI accelerators like Huawei's Ascend and Cambricon's products. This positions SMIC in a strong seller's market.

Other Chinese foundries are also experiencing growth, with Hua Hong reporting record revenue and high utilization. Foundry prices across China have seen increases, reflecting a broader trend in the global semiconductor industry, but SMIC's position is unique due to its captive customer base.

Chinese AI chip companies, including Cambricon, Moore Threads, and Biren, have reported substantial revenue growth and are pursuing IPOs. Memory maker CXMT also saw a massive surge in its stock value after its Shanghai listing.

headline: Hyperscalers are toast if this Hacker News report is true
summary: A recent Hacker News discussion suggests a significant shift in cloud computing infrastructure, potentially disrupting major hyperscale providers.
details: A discussion on Hacker News has ignited speculation about the future of cloud computing, with users suggesting that current hyperscale providers could face significant disruption.
The core of the speculation revolves around a potential paradigm shift in how cloud infrastructure is managed and utilized, though specific details remain unconfirmed.

While the exact nature of the threat is not fully elaborated, the sentiment suggests a fundamental change that could challenge the dominance of current market leaders like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
The conversation highlights a growing sentiment among some tech observers that the current model of hyperscale cloud services may not be sustainable or optimal in the long term.
